unallocated-exposure: No actor or protection layer clearly bears the loss class.
allocated-by-contract: Responsibility has been assigned by contract but recovery may remain uncertain.
coverage-attached: A policy, bond, warranty, guarantee, escrow, or fund appears capable of response.
certificate-evidence-accepted: A workflow accepted a certificate or proof artifact as sufficient evidence.
endorsement-required: Protection depends on a rider, endorsement, additional-insured status, waiver, or special term.
nonresponsive-protection: A visible protection artifact exists but does not respond to the relevant loss.
condition-precedent-pending: Coverage or warranty response depends on an unmet condition.
warranty-breached: A representation, maintenance promise, or proof-quality warranty has failed.
notice-clock-running: A reporting duty has started and must be completed or accepted.
materiality-determination-pending: A financial, securities, or reporting materiality decision is open.
trigger-disputed: Parties disagree about whether the event meets the trigger grammar.
coverage-position-reserved: The responder is preserving coverage/warranty defenses.
defense-under-reservation: Defense or response is funded while rights are reserved.
exclusion-flagged: A non-covered or excluded class is plausible enough to route workflow.
exclusion-final: Protection is determined not to respond.
control-rights-disputed: Parties dispute who controls defense, settlement, remediation, recall, or repair.
deductible-unmet: The retained deductible layer has not yet been crossed.
sir-open: Self-insured retention is absorbing first loss.
aggregate-approaching: Accumulated losses are nearing an aggregate cap.
reserve-held: Capital, accounting reserve, escrow, bond, or holdback remains locked.
reserve-release-pending: Release depends on additional evidence, time, or sign-off.
indemnity-chain-mapped: Pass-through responsibility has been traced across counterparties.
subrogation-preserved: Evidence and notice preserve recovery rights after payment.
subrogation-impaired: Recovery rights are weakened by late notice, destroyed evidence, waiver, or settlement.
loss-run-sensitive: The event may affect future underwriting, price, limits, exclusions, or eligibility.
renewal-restricted: Renewal is conditioned on remediation, exclusions, higher retentions, or lower limits.
tail-open: Exposure remains live after transaction, incident, correction, sale, closure, or release.
claim-closed: Claim or exposure has a closed state with reopening/archive rules.
